outcome: The general Overfull Conjecture (simple graphs, Δ(G) > n/3) remains open, but in July 2026 it was fully proved for the special case Δ(G) = 4, and separately confirmed asymptotically for large graphs that are robust expanders with Δ(G) at least (1+ε)/2 times the order; a December 2025 preprint also tightened a sufficient condition implying the conjecture's conclusion for Δ-critical graphs.
summary: The Overfull Conjecture (Chetwynd & Hilton, 1986: a simple graph G with Δ(G) > |V(G)|/3 is Class 2 iff it contains an overfull subgraph H with Δ(H)=Δ(G)) is still open in general as of 22 September 2026, but has seen genuine partial progress within the window, all via traditional structural/combinatorial mathematics with no AI involvement of any kind. (1) Chen, McDonald & Shan, 'Towards the Overfull Conjecture II' (arXiv:2607.02270, submitted 2 July 2026), a sequel to Shan's solo 2023/2024 paper 'Towards the Overfull Conjecture' (arXiv:2308.16808, v4 revised 5 Sep 2024, later published in J. Graph Theory), confirms the conjecture for robust expanders meeting density criteria and, as a corollary, for all sufficiently large n with Δ(G) ≥ (1+ε)n/2 — an asymptotic special case restricting to large, dense graphs. (2) Ge, Gutin & Qi, 'Edge-chromatic 4-critical graphs and Overfull Conjecture for graphs with maximum degree 4' (arXiv:2607.10947, v1 12 Jul 2026, v2 31 Jul 2026), gives a complete structural proof of the conjecture restricted to Δ(G)=4 (Theorem 1, verbatim: 'Let G be a graph of order n with Δ(G)=4>n/3. Then G is a Class 2 graph if and only if G contains an overfull subgraph H with Δ(H)=4'), a genuine full resolution of one case, not the general conjecture. (3) Qi, Ge & Feng, 'A new improvement to the Overfull Conjecture' (arXiv:2512.07044, submitted 7 Dec 2025), tightens a prior sufficient condition (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan 2022) under which Δ-critical graphs are proved overfull, from Δ(G)−7δ(G)/4 ≥ (3n−17)/4 to Δ(G)−5δ(G)/3 ≥ (2n−7)/3 — an incremental narrowing of a technical gap, closer in character to progress on a lemma than a case settled outright, but it does restrict a nonempty class of graphs. All three papers were checked directly (abstract, and for the Δ=4 paper the full abstract and available text); none mentions AI, machine learning, computer search, or automated theorem proving of any kind — all describe purely structural/theoretical proofs. A fourth item flagged by triage, Plantholt & Shan's 'On the Multigraph Overfull Conjecture' (J. Graph Theory 2025, arXiv:2302.13197, preprint predates the window but journal publication in 2025 falls inside it), concerns a distinct multigraph analogue of the conjecture (due to Stiebitz et al.) with a different overfull definition depending on edge multiplicity r — this is a related/variant problem, not a case of the stated simple-graph conjecture, and is excluded from the status determination per §3.1. The current Wikipedia article 'Overfull graph' (checked directly, last modified 19 October 2025) still describes the conjecture as unsolved and does not reflect the Δ=4 resolution, which postdates that revision. Status is coded 'partial' on the strength of the Δ=4 resolution (arXiv:2607.10947), which is the most scope-clean, complete case settled in the window; direction is 'confirmed' since the settled case (Δ=4) came out affirming the conjecture's conclusion (Class 2 iff overfull subgraph exists), not refuting it.
competing_reading: One could argue the December 2025 bound-tightening (2512.07044) is too technical/incremental to count as a distinct 'partial' event and belongs folded into 'progress' instead, since it modifies a sufficient condition for a lemma-like corollary rather than settling a clearly delineated case of the conjecture itself; if so, the record's primary event would rest solely on the Δ=4 paper, which does not change the overall status coding but would change which papers anchor 'progress' language in a stricter reading. Also arguable: the Δ=4 preprint (arXiv:2607.10947, as of writing) has not yet been digested by outside experts or accepted at a journal, so a stricter reading might prefer treating it as 'claimed' rather than folding it into 'partial' without qualification — I have treated a settled special case backed by a full, explicit, checkable proof (a clean structural theorem for a fixed small parameter) as 'partial' per §6.1's framing that 'partial' means a case of the problem settled, independent of expert digestion, but the proof itself has not been vetted by a third party as of this research.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion, journal acceptance, or independent verification of arXiv:2607.10947's proof for Δ=4 would confirm that case is solid; resolution of the general conjecture (all Δ > n/3) would require either a full proof or a counterexample, neither of which has appeared.

judgement.doubts: All three post-snapshot events are case settlements (partial regardless of review); none uses AI. The Δ=4 and robust-expander results are both partial with no AI, so the choice between them does not affect the codes. The multigraph paper is a variant and is excluded. The bullet says Δ ≥ n/3 while the record and papers use Δ > n/3; immaterial here.
